text: A (straight-line) drawn at right-angles to the diameter of a circle, from its end, will fall outside the circle. And another straight-line cannot be inserted into the space between the (aforementioned) straight-line and the circumference. And the angle of the semi-circle is greater than any acute rectilinear angle whatsoever, and the remaining (angle is) less (than any acute rectilinear angle). Let $ABC$ be a circle around the center $D$ and the diameter $AB$. I say that the (straight-line) drawn from $A$, at right-angles to $AB$ [Prop~1.11], from its end, will fall outside the circle.
For (if) not (then), if possible, let it fall inside, like $CA$ (in the figure),
assertion: suppose the line falls inside the circle, like CA

frame.supposition: the (straight-line) drawn from $A$ falls inside the circle

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: let it fall inside, like $CA$ (in the figure)

text: and let $DC$ be joined.
Since $DA$ is equal to $DC$, angle $DAC$ is also equal to angle $ACD$ [Prop.~1.5].
assertion: angle DAC equals angle ACD

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: angle $DAC$ is also equal to angle $ACD$

text: And $DAC$ (is) a right-angle.
assertion: DAC is a right-angle

text: Thus, $ACD$ (is) also a right-angle.
assertion: ACD is also a right-angle

text: So, in triangle $ACD$, the two angles $DAC$ and $ACD$ are equal to two right-angles.
assertion: in triangle ACD the two angles DAC and ACD are equal to two right-angles

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: the two angles $DAC$ and $ACD$ are equal to two right-angles

text: The very thing is impossible [Prop.~1.17].
assertion: contradiction

text: Thus, the (straight-line) drawn from point $A$, at right-angles to $BA$, will not fall inside the circle.
assertion: the line from A at right-angles to BA will not fall inside the circle

frame.closes: the (straight-line) drawn from $A$ falls inside the circle

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: the (straight-line) drawn from point $A$, at right-angles to $BA$, will not fall inside the circle

text: So, similarly, we can show that neither (will it fall) on the circumference.
assertion: similarly, the line will not fall on the circumference

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: So, similarly, we can show that neither (will it fall) on the circumference

text: Thus, (it will fall) outside (the circle).
assertion: the line falls outside the circle

text: Let it fall like $AE$ (in the figure).
So, I say that another straight-line cannot be inserted into the space between the straight-line $AE$ and the circumference $CHA$.
For, if possible, let it be inserted like $FA$ (in the figure),
assertion: suppose another line FA is inserted between AE and the circumference

frame.supposition: another straight-line can be inserted between the straight-line $AE$ and the circumference $CHA$

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: let it be inserted like $FA$ (in the figure)

text: and let $DG$ be drawn from point $D$, perpendicular to $FA$ [Prop.~1.12].
And since $AGD$ is a right-angle, and $DAG$ (is) less than a right-angle, $AD$ (is) thus greater than $DG$ [Prop.~1.19].
assertion: AD is greater than DG

text: And $DA$ (is) equal to $DH$.
assertion: DA equals DH

text: Thus, $DH$ (is) greater than $DG$, the lesser than the greater.
assertion: DH is greater than DG (the lesser than the greater)

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: $DH$ (is) greater than $DG$, the lesser than the greater

text: The very thing is impossible.
assertion: contradiction

text: Thus, another straight-line cannot be inserted into the space between the straight-line ($AE$) and the circumference.
assertion: no straight-line can be inserted between AE and the circumference

frame.closes: another straight-line can be inserted between the straight-line $AE$ and the circumference $CHA$

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: another straight-line cannot be inserted into the space between the straight-line ($AE$) and the circumference

text: And I also say that the semi-circular angle contained by the straight-line $BA$ and the circumference $CHA$ is greater than any acute rectilinear angle whatsoever, and the remaining (angle) contained by the circumference $CHA$ and the straight-line $AE$ is less than any acute rectilinear angle whatsoever.

For if any rectilinear angle is greater than the (angle) contained by the straight-line $BA$ and the circumference $CHA$, or less than the (angle) contained by the circumference $CHA$ and the straight-line $AE$, (then) a straight-line can be inserted into the space between the circumference $CHA$ and the straight-line $AE$---anything which will make (an angle) contained by straight-lines greater than the angle contained by the straight-line $BA$ and the circumference $CHA$, or less than the (angle) contained by the circumference $CHA$ and the straight-line $AE$.
assertion: if any rectilinear angle exceeds the semi-circular horn angle or is less than the curvilinear angle, then a straight-line can be inserted

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: if any rectilinear angle is greater than the (angle) contained by the straight-line $BA$ and the circumference $CHA$, or less than the (angle) contained by the circumference $CHA$ and the straight-line $AE$, (then) a straight-line can be inserted into the space between the circumference $CHA$ and the straight-line $AE$---anything which will make (an angle) contained by straight-lines greater than the angle contained by the straight-line $BA$ and the circumference $CHA$, or less than the (angle) contained by the circumference $CHA$ and the straight-line $AE$

text: But (such a straight-line) cannot be inserted.
assertion: such a straight-line cannot be inserted

text: Thus, an acute (angle) contained by straight-lines cannot be greater than the angle contained by the straight-line $BA$ and the circumference $CHA$,
assertion: an acute rectilinear angle cannot be greater than the semi-circular horn angle

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: an acute (angle) contained by straight-lines cannot be greater than the angle contained by the straight-line $BA$ and the circumference $CHA$

text: neither (can it be) less than the (angle) contained by the circumference $CHA$ and the straight-line $AE$.
assertion: neither can an acute rectilinear angle be less than the curvilinear angle

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: neither (can it be) less than the (angle) contained by the circumference $CHA$ and the straight-line $AE$

text: So, from this, (it is) manifest that a (straight-line) drawn at right-angles to the diameter of a circle, from its extremity, touches the circle [and that the straight-line touches the circle at a single point, inasmuch as it was also shown that a (straight-line) meeting (the circle) at two (points) falls inside it [Prop.~3.2]\,].
assertion: a line drawn at right-angles to the diameter from its extremity touches the circle (tangent)

spans.label: glue
spans.text: So, from this, (it is) manifest that

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: a (straight-line) drawn at right-angles to the diameter of a circle, from its extremity, touches the circle [and that the straight-line touches the circle at a single point, inasmuch as it was also shown that a (straight-line) meeting (the circle) at two (points) falls inside it [Prop.~3.2]\,]

text: (Which is) the very thing it was required to show.
